source.title: Dopamine transients encode reward prediction errors independent of learning rates.

confidence_rationale: High-quality causal-grade measurement (fiber-photometry dopamine in NAcc core during a volatile, semi-observable-state task) that confirms the supporting half of ARC-108 -- dopamine release does encode a signed RPE -- while complicating the naive teaching-signal story: dopamine encodes RPE INDEPENDENT of the dynamic learning rate, implying dopamine-independent mechanisms set how fast corticostriatal weights actually update. Mixed because it supports 'dopamine = signed RPE teaching signal' but weakens the assumption that the dopamine signal alone carries the full weight-update (RPE x learning-rate) that ARC-108's three-factor rule would compute as dopamine x eligibility.
failure_signatures: If ARC-108 implements the gating update as simply (dopamine RPE) x (fixed gain), it will mis-model the biology: the learning rate here is dynamic, scales with belief change at hidden-state transitions, and is instantiated by mechanisms OTHER than the dopamine transient.

A three-factor rule whose only adaptive term is dopamine cannot reproduce state-transition-driven learning-rate increases; ARC-108 needs the postsynaptic/eligibility factor (or an explicit belief-state gain) to carry the dynamic learning rate, not the dopamine signal.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a volatile task with semi-observable states, rats set dynamic learning rates that rise at state transitions and scale with trial-by-trial belief changes (approximating Bayesian updating), yet nucleus-accumbens-core dopamine release encodes the reward-prediction error INDEPENDENT of the learning rate -- so dopamine reflects RPE, not RPE x learning-rate, and dopamine-independent mechanisms instantiate the dynamic learning rate.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports ARC-108's premise that dopamine carries a signed RPE teaching signal, but warns that the learning rate (how much that RPE actually moves the gating weight) is set elsewhere. For ARC-108's three-factor rule, this argues the dynamic-gain role must live in the postsynaptic/eligibility factor or an explicit belief-state term, not be folded into the dopamine signal.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Measured in nucleus accumbens core (a value/limbic striatal region), not the dorsal/associative striatum most relevant to ARC-108's committed-selection gating; rodent fiber-photometry is bulk release, not per-synapse. The dissociation may differ in the dorsal gating circuit.
mapping.source_context: Rats performing a volatile, semi-observable-state reward task; NAcc-core dopamine via genetically-encoded sensor + fiber photometry; computational (Bayesian/RL) modeling of behaviour.

confidence_components.notes: Strong measurement; mapping_fidelity moderate because the nuance (RPE independent of learning rate) bears on ARC-108's rule decomposition rather than refuting the substrate; region (NAcc core vs dorsal gating) raises transfer risk.
